title: Finite concatenation of operadic colimit cocones
statement:
Use monoidal infinity categories of [def-coef-monoidal-infinity-category], small simplicial sets and coherent functors of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], and active cocones, concatenation $\oplus$ and weak operadic colimits of [def-coef-operadic-correspondence]. For this nonsymmetric assertion use the following explicit stability hypothesis, stronger than the separate one-sided tests in that definition: an active cocone $c:K^{\triangleright}\to\mathcal V^\otimes_{\mathrm{act}}$, with apex a tuple of any length, is stable in all contexts if $L\oplus c\oplus R$ is weakly operadically colimiting for every pair of finite tuples $L,R$, either of which may be empty. Explicitly, for every color $w\in\mathcal V$, precomposition with this contextual cocone must induce an equivalence from active arrows $L\oplus c(\infty)\oplus R\to w$ to coherent active cocones $L\oplus c|_K\oplus R\to w$.

Let $r\geq0$ and let $c_i:K_i^{\triangleright}\to\mathcal V^\otimes_{\mathrm{act}}$, $1\leq i\leq r$, be active cocones stable in all contexts in an arbitrary monoidal infinity category. Put $K=\prod_iK_i$. Then the cocone
$$K^{\triangleright}\longrightarrow\prod_iK_i^{\triangleright}\xrightarrow{\prod_i c_i}(\mathcal V^\otimes_{\mathrm{act}})^r\xrightarrow{\oplus}\mathcal V^\otimes_{\mathrm{act}}$$
is stable in all contexts, and hence is operadically colimiting according to the one-sided tests of [def-coef-operadic-correspondence]. Its apex is the ordered concatenation of the apices of the $c_i$. For $r=0$, $K=\Delta^0$ and this is the constant identity cocone on the empty tuple. Empty $K_i$ are allowed. No existence of other colimits and no global preservation of colimits by tensoring is assumed.

source.place: Proposition 3.1.1.8, printed pp. 321–322; GH Proposition A.2.4. Nonsymmetric formulation following Gepner–Haugseng, arXiv:1312.3178v4 Appendix A. Read online; archive WANTED. No Stacks tag states this infinity-categorical fact.

proof.text: Write $A=\mathcal V^\otimes_{\mathrm{act}}$ and $v_i=c_i(\infty)$. The map $K^{\triangleright}\to\prod_iK_i^{\triangleright}$ is the product of the join-cone extensions of the projections $K\to K_i$: each projection sends the new final vertex to the final vertex. Composing with the given cocones and concatenation gives exactly the displayed cocone, whose vertex is $v_1\oplus\cdots\oplus v_r$. Concatenation and the supplied monoidal coherences also give the diagrams with fixed contexts $L,R$. Thus no choice of a colimit object is being used. The hypothesis in this item supplies weak operadic universality for every such pair of contexts, not merely for the two separate one-sided cases.

source.place: Proposition 3.1.1.8, displayed product-cone construction; GH A.2.4, with the explicit contextual correction in the item statement.

proof.text:
We first identify active cocone spaces with ordinary cocone spaces after total tensoring. For a tuple $u$ over $[n]$, take a $p$-cocartesian edge $e_u:u\to t_u$ above the unique active map $[n]\to[1]$. Such a lift exists by the monoidal-category definition, also for $n=0$. Its target is the total tensor of $u$. By the cocartesian mapping-square criterion, the fiber of precomposition over this unique active base arrow gives
$$\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal V}(t_u,w)\simeq\operatorname{Map}_{A}(u,w)\qquad(w\in\mathcal V).$$
Indeed the left base fiber is over $\mathrm{id}_{[1]}$, and the right base fiber is over $[n]\to[1]$; each is a fiber over one point of a discrete base mapping space. The color inclusion $j:\mathcal V\hookrightarrow A$ is fully faithful, since the only active endomorphism of $[1]$ is its identity. Apply the opposite assertion of parametric universal arrows to $j$ and these universal edges. It assembles them into a coherent left adjoint $\tau:A\to\mathcal V$, with unit $u\to j\tau u$, and gives, for every small simplicial set $B$ and diagram $a:B\to A$, the natural equivalence
$$\operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{Fun}(B,\mathcal V)}(\tau a,\Delta_Bw)\simeq\operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{Fun}(B,A)}(a,\Delta_Bj w).$$
The equivalence commutes with restriction of $B$ and with the maps induced by cocone legs. The dual cocone criterion of [lem-cbc-enhanced-functor-cone-calculus] identifies ordinary colimits with precisely these fixed-target precomposition equivalences. Consequently an active join cocone is weakly operadically colimiting exactly when its image under $\tau$ is an ordinary colimit cocone in $\mathcal V$. The join-slice comparison identifies join cocones with these coherent transformation spaces, including the empty indexing shape. All functor categories can be formed in a containing universe.

source.place: Proposition 3.1.1.7, mapping-space reduction; GH Proposition A.2.6. Expanded through the existing universal-arrow and cocartesian mapping-square statements.

proof.text:
Here is the parameter restriction calculation used below. Let $B,D$ be small simplicial sets and $H:B\times D^{\triangleright}\to\mathcal V$ a coherent diagram, with $H_b:D^{\triangleright}\to\mathcal V$ colimiting for every vertex $b\in B$. Put $F=H|_{B\times D}$ and $G=H|_{B\times\{\infty\}}$. Transpose $H$ to $D^{\triangleright}\to\operatorname{Fun}(B,\mathcal V)$. The objectwise colimit criterion says this specified cocone is colimiting: all its required objectwise colimits are precisely the given $H_b$, so no other colimits in $\mathcal V$ are needed. Apply the dual fixed-target cocone criterion of [lem-cbc-enhanced-functor-cone-calculus] in this functor quasicategory. Its universal property at the constant diagram $\Delta_BT$, followed by transposing coherent transformations, is
$$\operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{Fun}(B,\mathcal V)}(G,\Delta_BT)\simeq\operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{Fun}(B\times D,\mathcal V)}(F,\Delta_{B\times D}T).$$
For precision, the exponential identification $\operatorname{Fun}(D,\operatorname{Fun}(B,\mathcal V))\cong\operatorname{Fun}(B\times D,\mathcal V)$ sends a degree-$m$ simplex to the same map $B\times D\times\Delta^m\to\mathcal V$, after permuting the factors. Applied to the right-pinched mapping spaces, a degree-$n$ simplex on either side is a map $B\times D\times\Delta^{n+1}\to\mathcal V$ whose entire initial face $B\times D\times\Delta^{\{0,\ldots,n\}}$ is the constant family at $F$ and whose last-vertex restriction is $\Delta_{B\times D}T$. The simplicial operators on both sides extend $[m]\to[n]$ by the new last vertex. Thus this identification respects the specified source, target and every higher simplex. The displayed comparison sends a cocone $G\to T$ to its composite with the $D$-direction legs of $H$. This calculation includes $B=\varnothing$ and $D=\varnothing$.

source.place: Proposition 3.1.1.8, binary proof and its Lemma 3.1.1.9: in the monoidal case, the needed parameter restriction follows from the existing pointwise colimit criterion and the defining exponential formula.

proof.text:
Prove the binary case. Fix arbitrary tuples $L,R$, let $c_1:B^{\triangleright}\to A$ and $c_2:D^{\triangleright}\to A$ have vertices $v_1,v_2$, and set
$$H(b,t)=\tau\bigl(L\oplus c_1(b)\oplus c_2(t)\oplus R\bigr).$$
For every vertex $b$ of $B$, this is the image under $\tau$ of $c_2$ with left context $L\oplus c_1(b)$ and right context $R$. The hypothesis on $c_2$ and Step 2 show $H_b$ is colimiting. Step 3 therefore gives the restriction equivalence from cocones on $G(b)=\tau(L\oplus c_1(b)\oplus v_2\oplus R)$ to cocones on $F(b,d)=\tau(L\oplus c_1(b)\oplus c_2(d)\oplus R)$. The $c_1$ hypothesis, now with left context $L$ and right context $v_2\oplus R$, gives another equivalence
$$\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal V}\bigl(\tau(L\oplus v_1\oplus v_2\oplus R),T\bigr)\simeq\operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{Fun}(B,\mathcal V)}(G,\Delta_BT).$$
Compose the two equivalences for every color $T$. Their composite is precomposition with the displayed binary product cocone. In the order of the two restriction maps its leg is $(b,d)\to(b,\infty)\to(\infty,\infty)$: first the $c_2$ leg, then the $c_1$ leg. To compare this with the simultaneous leg, restrict the product of the two join cocones to the square $\Delta^1\times\Delta^1$ determined by these legs. The triangle with vertices $(0,0),(0,1),(1,1)$ gives a $2$-simplex identifying their composite with the diagonal $(0,0)\to(1,1)$, which is precisely the product-cocone leg in Step 1. Apply the concatenation functor, the fixed contexts and $\tau$ to this same triangle. Doing this after every simplicial restriction of the two diagrams gives the compatibility for coherent families of legs, since all these restrictions are restrictions of the single functor on $B^{\triangleright}\times D^{\triangleright}$. Naturality in Step 2 and the mapping-space identification in Step 3 therefore identify the composite restriction map with the map of the specified product cocone up to this coherent homotopy. By Step 2 this proves weak operadic universality of $L\oplus c\oplus R$. Since both contexts were arbitrary, the binary output is stable in all contexts.

source.place: Proposition 3.1.1.8, binary proof: first eliminate the second variable, then the first. Both contexts are retained throughout to repair the nonsymmetric gap in GH A.2.4.

proof.text: Induct on the number of inputs with the claim that the specified product cocone is stable in all contexts and has the ordered tuple of input vertices as apex. For one input the claim is its hypothesis. Given the claim for $s\geq1$ inputs, concatenate that output with $c_{s+1}$ using Step 4. The product identification $(\prod_{i\leq s}K_i)\times K_{s+1}=\prod_{i\leq s+1}K_i$ and the coherent associativity of concatenation identify its cocone and all its legs with those in Step 1; this proves the induction step. For zero inputs, the empty product is $\Delta^0$ and the cocone is constant with identity leg on the empty tuple. In every context it is still the identity cocone on $L\oplus R$; restriction of cocones is the identity on its active mapping space, so it is weakly operadically colimiting. This proves the induction base at zero directly. If a $K_i$ is empty, Step 3 still applies: a cocone on the empty diagram with fixed vertex is the one-point space, and no step chooses a vertex of that $K_i$. Thus the same binary argument and induction handle all empty factors. Finally choose $L$ or $R$ empty to recover both one-sided tests in the referenced definition, which proves the asserted operadic colimit conclusion.

source.place: Proposition 3.1.1.8, first paragraph (empty and singleton families, finite induction), with empty factors and the cone legs made explicit.
